title: Replacement Authorization After a Stalled Repair — Homeowner Service Contracts Claims Action
content:
## When this action applies

On a Bridgewell Homeowner Service Contract, a repair authorization stalls when it stands more than the tier's parts lead time (in calendar days) after its authorization date without a completion report. When the customer then declines the stalled repair and it is reversed, the parts are treated as not obtainable within that parts lead time, and Bridgewell replaces the item by issuing a replacement authorization on the same request with the replacement basis "parts unavailable", carrying the covered item and the repair estimate recorded on the reversed repair authorization, and recording as its replacement cost the re-priced like-unit cost and as its amount the stalled-repair replacement payment.

The replacement is Bridgewell's decision under the repair-or-replace standard; it is recorded by the agent on the customer's existing service request, not on a new one.

## Business effect

The replacement authorization is added to the request's claim-handling history with a new authorization number and the basis "parts unavailable". The amount recorded is what Bridgewell commits toward the replacement, and it counts against the contract's benefits from the day it is recorded.

## How it is invoked

The tool is `authorize_stalled_repair_replacement_b6f80e12`. It is an agent-side tool: the agent unlocks it and then calls it.

## Parameters

| Parameter | Meaning | Format |
|---|---|---|
| `homeplan_contract_id` | the homeowner service contract number the request is placed under, as returned by the homeowner contract lookup | identifier |
| `homeplan_service_request_id` | the service request number of the failed item being replaced, as returned by the service request or claim-history lookup | identifier |
| `covered_item` | the item being replaced | one value from the list below |
| `repair_estimate` | the contractor's repair estimate that was compared | USD, rounded to 2 decimal places, positive |
| `replacement_cost` | the like-unit cost (equipment plus installation) to record on the authorization as its replacement cost | USD, rounded to 2 decimal places, positive |
| `amount` | the amount Bridgewell commits toward the replacement | USD, rounded to 2 decimal places, positive |

Values accepted for `covered_item`: `heating_system` (the furnace, boiler or heat pump heating side), `cooling_system` (the central air conditioning), `ductwork` (heating and cooling ducts), `plumbing_leak` (an interior water supply or drain leak), `plumbing_stoppage` (an interior drain stoppage), `water_heater` (the water heater), `electrical` (the interior electrical system), `ceiling_fan` (a ceiling fan), `garbage_disposal` (the garbage disposal), `whirlpool_tub` (the whirlpool bathtub motor and pump), `refrigerator` (the kitchen refrigerator), `oven_range_cooktop` (the oven, range or cooktop), `dishwasher` (the dishwasher), `built_in_microwave` (the built-in microwave), `clothes_washer` (the clothes washer), `clothes_dryer` (the clothes dryer), `garage_door_opener` (the garage door opener).

## Return

On success the tool returns a confirmation with `authorization_number` (the new replacement authorization number), `homeplan_service_request_id` (the request it was issued on), `covered_item` (the item replaced), `replacement_basis` (always `parts_unavailable`), `amount` (USD, 2 decimal places) and `status`, which reads "authorized" when the authorization was recorded. The request then shows the new replacement authorization with its number, basis and amount.

## Contract notes

- **What does one call record?** One replacement authorization with the basis "parts unavailable" and a new authorization number; nothing else on the request is changed by the call.
- **Which repair estimate is recorded?** The repair estimate recorded on the reversed repair authorization, carried onto the replacement.
